newsitem.title: BULGARIA: SOCCER-CLOUD HANGS OVER BULGARIAN CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CLOUD HANGS OVER BULGARIAN CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Bulgaria's soccer championship resumes this weekend overshadowed by a miserable performance by the country's two top teams in Europe.

Champions CSKA Sofia, who in the past have produced players of the quality of Hristo Stoichkov and Emil Kostadinov, failed in the European Cup qualifying round when they went down 2-0 to Romania's Steaua Bucharest in Sofia on Wednesday, losing 5-3 on aggregate.
Neftochimik Bourgas, second in the championship last season, lost their UEFA Cup preliminary round tie on the same night on the away goals rule despite beating Norway's Brann Bergen 3-2 in Bourgas.

Bulgarian soccer supporters have been left clinging to the hope that Levski Sofia will do better at home to Slovakia's Slovan Bratislava in a European Cup Winners Cup qualifying round tie on August 14.
"It is clear...that European work can not be done with a provincial mentality," sports newspaper Seven Days Sport said on Thursday, refering to CSKA's performance.
Neftochimik Bourgas lost their sponsor this week when the new management of the debt-ridden Neftochim oil refinery said it could no longer back the club due to a lack of funds.

The plant spent some 1.5 billion levs ($818,000) on Neftochimik in 1996 and the first five months of this year, and built a modern football stadium in Bourgas at a cost of 1.9 billion levs ($1 million).
Club president Hristo Portochanov said the club would now be forced to sell their top player and captain Radostin Kishishev.
However, on a brighter note for the new season, soccer analysts expect surprises from the three newcomers in the first division, Litex Lovech, Metalurg Pernik and Olympic Galata.
Levski Sofia's new coach Stefan Grozdanov forecast Litex would be among six teams battling for the championship.
Apart from his own team, he said the others involved in the title race would be CSKA Sofia, Slavia Sofia, Lokomotiv Sofia and Neftochimik Bourgas.
